question: Why does opening more checkouts help most when any cashier can serve any customer?
options: Because more checkouts always cost less than a faster cashier
Because a customer who must return to one particular cashier cannot be sent to whichever checkout is free
Because customers prefer the same cashier every time
explanation: This is stateless scaling. If a server must keep the user's data in its own memory, the balancer has to send that user back to the same server, so a free server cannot help them. Sticky sessions can make this work, but less flexibly. Cost is a separate question.
